(1) users do not always read the results they look at; (2) there are two distinct stages in the examination process: a skimming stage and a reading stage; (3) the two-stage examination process is related to mouse movement; and (4) the two-stage model is better for predicting user examination behavior and estimating result relevance than a single-stage model

(1) a large proportion (about 45.8%) results fixated by the users are not recognized by users as being "read"; (2) the two-stage examination behavior can be captured with mouse movements; (3) the two-stage model outperforms single-stage model for estimating user's relevance judgment.

1) a large proportion of results fixated by a user may not be recognized as being "examined" by the user; 2) there is a "skimming to reading" step in the examination process; 3) the examination process can be predicted using mouse movement information; and 4) the two-stage examination process has a significant impact on search engine relevance estimation.
